DatasetIntro: Prepare voices from multiple recordings. Originals and previous versions are preserved.
SampleTips: Use one clear speaker with little music. Vary phrases and intonations; aim for several dozen seconds. Avoid clipping. Music and other speakers are not automatically classified.
ReferenceLimit: Your full dataset is retained. Studio pools speaker identity from up to 64 reference segments, with at most 25 seconds per reference. This does not train a personal model.
SimilarityTip: Lower keeps more original timbre. Higher guides the model toward the target and may increase artifacts. Recommended: 70%. Separate from speed.
PerformanceTip: Expressive: fixed 20 / 30 / 40 steps. Conversation: initial 4 / 6 / 8 steps, measured window at voice load; adaptation only in pauses. Direct: 6 / 12 / 24 steps.
ComputeTip: Auto uses CUDA if available, otherwise CPU. Microphone source remains available. CPU may be too slow for live use. DirectML is unsupported.
DynamicsTip: Follows relative volume and pauses in Keep my intonation mode and in the classic engine. Reference expression keeps the generated rhythm.
CpuRealtimeWarning: Processing cannot keep up: normal voice restored to avoid growing delay. Try Low latency or CUDA.
QuickVoiceTip: Switch between clean and the last selected voice.
LastSound: Open the last sound controls without replaying it.
BassTip: Lower: less rumble. Higher: warmer, potentially muddy. Recommended: 0 dB.
MidTip: Controls presence and nasal character. Recommended: 0 dB.
TrebleTip: Lower: softer. Higher: brighter, more hiss. Recommended: 0 dB.
GateTip: Lower threshold preserves quiet sounds. Higher removes more noise but may cut speech. Recommended: −48 dB.
CompressorTip: Reduces quiet/loud differences. More compression is steadier but less natural. Recommended: 3:1.
CpuMayBeSlow: CPU selected: measuring performance. Normal voice takes over if processing is too slow.
SoundClickHelp: Click to play. Right-click to preview, organize or edit.

Ui498: 0 dB is neutral. Frequencies 20–20,000 Hz; low Q means a wider band. The limiter stays active after EQ.
Ui499: ASIO uses the actual buffer size selected in its driver.
Ui500: Treble adds clarity but may emphasize sibilance.
Ui501: Treble: negative softens, positive brightens. Start at 0 dB.
Ui502: Adds intentional distortion for a dense, compressed sound with vibrating bass. Zero adds no saturation. The final limiter prevents digital overload.
Ui503: Gradually adjusts speech level. May amplify background noise; leave disabled if your level is consistent.
Ui504: Raises input level. Start at 0 dB; use calibration to avoid clipping.
Ui505: Auto selects NVIDIA graphics when available. CUDA uses it to accelerate voice processing. CPU processes phrases with more delay. This engine does not support OpenCL.
Ui507: Select CABLE Output as microphone to receive Virtual Mic. Use a second virtual output to isolate Stream Mix. Do not assign two buses to the same device.
Ui508: Cuts very quiet sounds. A higher threshold removes more noise but can cut softly spoken words.
Ui509: Direct prioritizes low latency. Conversation uses continuous contextual processing, recommended for Discord if the performance test passes. Expressive transfers style in phrases up to 8 seconds, recommended for files. CPU throughput may be insufficient.
Ui510: Bass adds body or reduces a muffled voice.
Ui511: Bass: negative lightens, positive thickens. Start at 0 dB.
Ui512: Isolates this channel in headphones. The virtual microphone and recordings continue normally.
Ui513: Light preserves more detail; Strong removes more noise but can color the voice.
Ui514: Monitor plays the captured copy. If Windows already plays this application in your headphones, disable Monitor to avoid doubled sound.
Ui516: Midrange: negative scoops, positive brings forward. Start at 0 dB.
Ui517: Mix: 0 dry voice, 100 full effect. Start at 100%.
Ui518: Number of simultaneous CPU tasks. Higher values may slow other applications. Changes apply on the next engine start.
Ui519: A higher ratio reduces loud passages more. Recommended starting point: 3:1.
Ui520: Recording Mix selects multiple channels in the matrix. Recording starts after you choose a WAV file.
Ui521: Boosts low frequencies. This setting is saved for this sound.
Ui522: Rule saved with the channel and profiles, even after the application closes. Takes priority over the matrix.
Ui523: Reduces steady noise. A high setting may alter timbre; start with Low.
Ui524: Reduces differences between loud and quiet passages. Output gain can compensate afterward.
Ui525: Saturation: 0 disabled, 100 strongly clipped. Start at 0%.
Ui526: Studio uses Seed-VC V2 style transfer. Adaptive selects a reference using energy and pitch variation from your voice and samples. It does not understand the meaning of words. Identity is pooled across up to 64 references.
Ui527: Each row is a source; each column is an output. An enabled switch sends sound to that destination. Stream and Recording can stay internal.
Ui528: WASAPI is recommended. ASIO appears only when a driver is installed. This engine does not provide WDM/KS.
Ui529: Echo: 0 disabled, 100 very prominent. Start at 0%.

ModeDirectTip: Lowest latency, with less context and expression. Suits quick exchanges and less powerful hardware. CPU processing may still be too slow.
ModeConversationTip: Continuous audio with more context and the V2 vocoder. Suits Discord and gaming if your voice benchmark confirms sufficient speed. Preserves your prosody; does not regenerate AR style.
ModeExpressiveTip: Style transfer and high quality, with a substantial delay. Recommended for recordings and files; microphone input is processed in phrases.
